title: General insurance value measures data
text: The Financial Conduct Authority publishes general insurance value measures data covering claims frequencies, claims acceptance rates, average claim payouts and claims complaints as a proportion of claims. Reporting covers home, home emergency, motor, travel, personal accident, gadget, tyre and key cover products. Firms submit data twice yearly. The data is intended to let consumers and commentators compare the value delivered by different products rather than price alone. Claims acceptance rates vary materially between product categories, with add-on products typically showing lower acceptance than core cover. The FCA has noted that a low claims acceptance rate is not automatically evidence of poor value, because exclusions may be clearly disclosed, but persistent outliers warrant supervisory attention.

title: Pet insurance market statistics
text: Association of British Insurers data on the pet insurance market reports gross written premium, policy counts and average premiums across lifetime, time-limited and accident-only cover. The market has grown steadily as pet ownership increased, with lifetime policies accounting for the majority of gross written premium. Average premiums have risen faster than general inflation. Only a minority of UK pets are insured, which commentators cite as evidence of headroom, though uninsured owners frequently report that they intend to self-fund treatment. Gross written premium figures are reported on an annual basis and include both direct and intermediated distribution.

title: Solvency capital requirements
text: The Prudential Regulation Authority supervises the capital adequacy of UK insurers under the Solvency II framework as retained and amended in UK law. Firms must hold eligible own funds sufficient to cover the Solvency Capital Requirement, calibrated to a one-in-two-hundred-year loss over a one-year horizon. The Minimum Capital Requirement sits below the SCR and triggers the most severe supervisory interventions if breached. Firms may use the standard formula or, with approval, a full or partial internal model. The matching adjustment and the risk margin have been subject to reform, altering the capital treatment of long-dated annuity liabilities.

title: General insurance pricing practices
text: Following a market study into home and motor insurance pricing, the FCA introduced rules addressing price walking, where renewing customers are quoted more than equivalent new customers. The loyalty penalty was found to fall disproportionately on consumers who did not shop around, including those less able to engage with the market. Firms must now offer renewing customers a price no higher than the equivalent new business price for the same product through the same channel. The rules are accompanied by product governance requirements and reporting obligations, and firms must demonstrate that their pricing models do not reintroduce the practice by another route.

title: Motor insurance claims costs
text: Motor insurance claims costs have been driven upward by vehicle repair complexity, parts availability, paint and labour rates, and the increasing electronic content of modern vehicles. Calibration of advanced driver assistance sensors after a repair adds cost that did not exist on older vehicles. Credit hire and courtesy vehicle provision contribute to the total, as does personal injury settlement cost under the current discount rate. Theft claims have risen for certain models following keyless entry compromise. Insurers have responded with premium increases, tighter repair network management and greater use of salvage rather than repair.

title: Pet insurance claims trends
text: Veterinary fee inflation is the dominant driver of pet insurance claims cost. Consolidation of independent practices into corporate groups has coincided with higher prices for consultations, diagnostics and surgery. Advanced interventions once confined to referral centres, including MRI imaging and orthopaedic surgery, are now routinely claimed. Average claim size has risen faster than claim frequency, meaning severity rather than incidence explains most of the cost increase. The competition authority has examined the veterinary services market, and its findings bear directly on the sustainability of lifetime pet insurance pricing.

title: Market investigation references
text: The Competition and Markets Authority may make a market investigation reference where it has reasonable grounds to suspect that a feature of a market prevents, restricts or distorts competition. A market study precedes a reference and may conclude without one. An investigation can impose remedies including divestment, price controls, information requirements and recommendations to government. Statutory deadlines govern each phase. Parties may apply to the Competition Appeal Tribunal for review of a decision, on judicial review grounds rather than a full rehearing of the merits.

title: Compensation when an insurer fails
text: The Financial Services Compensation Scheme protects policyholders if an authorised insurer is unable to meet claims. For compulsory classes, including motor third-party liability and employers' liability, protection is one hundred per cent of the claim with no upper limit. For most other general insurance, protection is ninety per cent of the claim with no upper limit. Long-term insurance, including annuities, is protected at one hundred per cent. Cover applies to the policy and claims rather than to a deposit balance, and eligibility depends on the claimant being an eligible person under the scheme rules.

title: Insurtech venture funding
text: Venture funding into insurance technology companies rose through a period of cheap capital and then contracted sharply as interest rates increased. Early-stage rounds proved more resilient than growth rounds. Managing general agent models attracted scrutiny after several high-profile retrenchments, with capacity providers withdrawing support where loss ratios disappointed. Distribution-led propositions fared better than full-stack carriers, which required regulatory capital and reinsurance relationships that proved difficult to secure at scale. Exit activity has been dominated by trade sales rather than public listings.

title: Insurance Premium Tax
text: Insurance Premium Tax applies to most general insurance premiums where the insured risk is located in the United Kingdom. There is a standard rate and a higher rate; the higher rate applies to travel insurance and to insurance sold alongside certain goods and services such as vehicles and domestic appliances. Long-term insurance, reinsurance and certain commercial marine, aviation and transport risks are exempt. Insurers register with HMRC and account for the tax on either a cash-received or a special accounting basis. The tax is a cost to the insurer that is generally passed through to the premium charged.

title: Travel insurance claims handling
text: Travel insurance claims are dominated by medical repatriation, cancellation and baggage. Medical costs in certain jurisdictions can exceed the headline policy limit, and insurers maintain assistance networks to manage treatment and transport. Cancellation claims cluster around named perils, and disputes commonly concern whether a pre-existing condition was disclosed. Baggage claims are low in value and high in frequency, with receipts and proof of ownership the usual friction. Claims handling is frequently outsourced to specialist administrators, which complicates complaint routing when a policyholder is dissatisfied with a decision.

title: Home emergency cover
text: Home emergency cover provides access to a tradesperson for boiler failure, plumbing leaks, electrical faults, pest infestation and lock replacement. It is sold as an add-on to buildings insurance and also as a standalone subscription. Cover is typically capped per claim and per policy year, with annual limits on call-outs. Exclusions commonly include pre-existing faults, systems beyond a stated age, and parts availability delays. Service quality depends on the contractor network rather than on the insurer, which is a frequent source of complaint.

title: Consumer Duty expectations
text: The Consumer Duty requires firms to act to deliver good outcomes for retail customers across products and services, price and value, consumer understanding and consumer support. Firms must identify their target market, test whether communications are understood, and evidence that support does not create unreasonable barriers. Boards are expected to receive an annual assessment. The duty is outcomes-focused rather than rules-based, which places the burden of demonstrating compliance on the firm's own monitoring and governance rather than on a checklist.

title: Pet ownership demographics
text: Household pet ownership is concentrated among families with children and among older households without dependants. Dogs and cats dominate, with smaller mammals, birds and fish accounting for the remainder. Ownership rose during periods of home working and then plateaued, with rehoming charities reporting higher intake afterwards. Urban households show lower dog ownership and higher cat ownership than rural households. Breed preferences shift with fashion, which has consequences for veterinary workload because some popular breeds are predisposed to specific conditions.

title: Veterinary workforce shortages
text: The veterinary profession reports persistent recruitment difficulty, particularly for experienced small-animal clinicians and for out-of-hours rotas. Registration of overseas-qualified vets has changed, altering supply. Retention is affected by on-call burden, client-facing conflict and the emotional weight of euthanasia decisions. Practices have responded with shift patterns, triage nursing and remote consultation. Workforce constraint limits appointment availability, which is distinct from the question of what treatment costs once an appointment is obtained.

title: Telematics in motor underwriting
text: Telematics underwriting uses driving data captured by a device or a phone to price risk on observed behaviour rather than on proxies. Acceleration, braking, cornering, speed relative to the limit and time of day are common inputs. Young drivers are the primary market because conventional rating penalises them heavily. Data governance questions include retention, secondary use and whether a score can be contested. Policyholders may find mid-term repricing or curfew conditions unexpected, which is a conduct consideration rather than a pricing one.

title: Reinsurance market conditions
text: Reinsurance pricing moves in cycles driven by catastrophe experience, available capital and investment returns. Retrocession capacity and insurance-linked securities influence the supply of limit at the top of programmes. Attachment points have risen, pushing frequency losses back onto primary carriers and changing the volatility that cedants retain. Treaty wording has tightened around communicable disease, cyber and strikes, riots and civil commotion. Renewal negotiations concentrate at the start of the year for European business.

title: Employers' liability insurance
text: Employers' liability insurance is compulsory for most employers and responds to claims by employees for injury or disease arising from employment. Long-tail exposures, notably asbestos-related disease, mean claims can emerge decades after the policy period. Tracing historic cover is a recognised difficulty, addressed through an industry tracing service and a database of policies. Certificates must be made available to employees. Premiums are rated on wage roll and occupation, with experience rating for larger accounts.

title: Guaranteed asset protection
text: Guaranteed asset protection pays the difference between a motor insurer's settlement and either the original purchase price or an outstanding finance balance. Distribution has historically been concentrated at the point of vehicle sale, where commission levels attracted regulatory attention and sales were paused while firms demonstrated value. Claim incidence is low because total losses are infrequent, which makes the value assessment turn on price relative to expected payout rather than on claims service.

title: Annuity rates for retirees
text: Annuity rates available to retirees move with gilt yields and with assumed longevity. Enhanced annuities offer higher income where medical or lifestyle factors shorten expected lifespan. Shopping around materially changes the income secured, yet many retirees buy from their existing pension provider. Options include single or joint life, guarantee periods, escalation and value protection, each reducing the starting income. The decision is irreversible once made, which is why the open market option is emphasised at the point of retirement.
